unmergedDoubts.whyNotMerged: Both answer "what happened to a child that was mid-flight at restart", but IH classifies an AMBIGUOUS in-flight attempt from the child log and never re-dispatches it, while dsh rebuilds a declared composition from a versioned descriptor and cold-resumes on purpose. One refuses to resume; the other exists to resume. Merging would hide that disagreement, so IH crash recovery stands alone (improved-writing on its own merits).

Both sit between a finished child and what the parent receives. dsh guarantees the RESULT SHAPE (a schema-validated value captured by two-phase commit, not the child text); IH guarantees DELIVERY (durable outbox, status re-check, suppression on cancelled chains). Result contract vs delivery contract; no source does both.

I deliberately split the model-facing coordination verbs into control (send/wait/interrupt/close/resume/list) and mailbox/delivery (turn-triggered mail, safe-point steer, team messaging). Most likely wrong merge in this domain, and the split is what forced codex inter-agent-mailbox and grok parent-wake to land in different rows. A reader who thinks send_message is one thing should merge rows subagent-coordination-control-surface and inter-agent-mailbox-and-messaging.

Same job concept from two ends. IH ships a projection with no store (durable snapshot doc + folded job/status events, plus a 409 kill vocabulary); dsh ships the registry itself (owner fencing, per-owner cap, first-wins settlement, wake budget). I kept the registry row pure, so IH background jobs have no registry member anywhere — read the two rows together.

I merged the team task boards (IH/dsh/cc) but NOT cc swarm-mailbox into the same row, because cc messaging is a polled file+in-process mailbox with a direct-message shortcut while IH/dsh treat the target session log or a target-side ack as the acknowledgement. Same sub-capability split as the mailbox doubt above.

IH task records are per-DELEGATION and live in a coordinator document keyed by a three-part identity; dsh Activation owns a per-CHILD residency with a child lock and an ownedChildren settlement gate. Same nouns (task, running, cancel) different objects. Kept apart so the durable task state machine row reads as one thing.

All three limit concurrent delegations but with different failure semantics: IH fails closed at submit, the fork acquires a permit before child creation and re-keys it, grok QUEUES by default and lets workflow-owned spawns bypass the quota entirely. The bypass is a design difference, not a gap, so grok admission stays its own row.

Both narrow what a child may do, but one narrows the TOOL INVENTORY by kind (and deliberately does not narrow kindless MCP/custom tools) while the other narrows the PERMISSION ruleset (only deny and external_directory inherit; todowrite/task default-deny). Capability inventory vs permission derivation.

Both are named workflow and both spawn children, but IH is a static sequential YAML registry where DAG/parallel/loops are deliberately NOT implemented, and dsh is a scripted worker-thread engine with agent/parallel/pipeline and per-run caps. Only the background-job wrapper is common; I declined to reconcile them on that.

All deliver text into a turn. codex makes mail a distinct TurnInput tier with a liveness gauge; grok admits a parent steer only at a turn-bound lifecycle point with a 32-slot bound; opencode wakes the parent by prompting it. I merged codex into durable-parent-wake-delivery and grok into inter-agent-mailbox and opencode into durable-parent-wake-delivery, so the safe-point/tiering nuance is spread across three rows rather than reconciled.

Placed as required, but neither is subagent-specific: scope routing is a core composition primitive and turn outline is a session-log projection, both of which several dsh subagent registries merely happen to sit on. If the sibling domain owners also place them, these two rows are duplicated across domains rather than unreconciled here.
